turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we'll keep this short. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay before anyone picked up a phone and called me?
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
This morning. The zero went in a week ago, so you reread them after you'd already decided. And you still haven't told me who made that call.
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. My reading habits aren't on the table, and you've now dodged the same question twice. Who decided?
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why are we here? A thoughtful kid with a zero, and nobody's told me on what basis.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.

It became a fight when Owen read that zero on his phone in the middle of class. Your own procedure, 4.2, says the parent is contacted before any mark goes in, and nobody contacted me. Either you show me what you're basing this on, or I walk down to the principal's office when we're done.
